issues.description: Getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field is inconsistent across artifacts. The template repository defines and uses getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" (implicitly expecting standard getter naming), which can cause confusion about which method name to implement and may lead to mismatches when students follow the template versus the intended solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field consistent across artifacts. Prefer the conventional getName() (update template StockIngredient to provide getName() and update any calls in Stock.findStockIngredient to use getName()), and ensure the problem statement's wording references the same getter naming convention. Alternatively, explicitly state allowed getter names to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The StockIngredient 'name' accessor is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template repository defines getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName(). Stock.findStockIngredient() implementations also call different getter names accordingly. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual field ('name' of a StockIngredient) creates unnecessary mapping friction for students trying to relate the template, problem description, and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts (prefer the conventional getName()). Update the template (rename getIngredientName() to getName()) and any callers (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) or alternatively change the solution to use getIngredientName(). Ensure the problem text and examples reflect the chosen name.
